issues.body: Section 6 says that a non-reader carrying a conditional precondition receives a denial instead of having the precondition evaluated, and lists If-Match/If-None-Match without qualification. The cited guard explicitly exempts a bare `*`: it gates only concrete entity-tag validators, because wildcard preconditions test existence and remain available to Write-without-Read callers. This omission materially misstates the security boundary and contradicts the document's claim to reconstruct the code accurately.
issues.fix_hint: Change the V4 row and surrounding description to say that concrete ETag validators are read-gated, while bare `If-Match: *` and `If-None-Match: *` are intentionally exempt; explain the implementation's stated rationale for that exemption.
issues.title: V4 table incorrectly says every conditional precondition is read-gated

issues.body: The new normative-spec section says Solid-OIDC access tokens and DPoP proofs are "not verified by this crate at all" and that the server "adds no acceptance of its own." Although full cache-miss verification is delegated, `src/auth_cache.rs` locally verifies DPoP proof signature and claims on cache hits, and `src/auth.rs` adds opt-in mTLS and DPoP-SK proof-of-possession paths. The absolute wording is therefore inaccurate and could mislead security integrators about which code and policies participate in request acceptance.
issues.fix_hint: State narrowly that baseline token/DPoP verification on the normal cache-miss path is delegated to the pinned verifier. Explicitly mention the local verified-token-cache DPoP hit path and the server's opt-in PoP tiers, and avoid claiming that the server adds no acceptance logic.
issues.title: Claim that the crate performs no DPoP verification is false

verdict.summary: The reconstructed design record is useful, but two claims do not match the current implementation. The V4 summary overstates which conditional requests are read-gated, and the usage skill incorrectly says this crate performs no Solid-OIDC DPoP verification or acceptance logic of its own. Both are security-relevant documentation errors and should be corrected before approval.
